detector._note: Keypoints 13-11-23 / 14-12-24 (elbow-shoulder-hip), vertex at the shoulder, 3D world angle. This is the angle the arm makes with the torso, not the bend of the elbow. Measured on traces/reference-shoulder-press.jsonl 6 Sep 2026: racked 53.6-55.1, locked out overhead 149.7-159.6, so a rep sweeps ~95 degrees of clear air. The elbow angle it replaced (11-13-15 / 12-14-16) only separated rack from lockout by 64 degrees and did it on the worst-observed segment: at lockout the forearm points down the camera axis, where the depth estimate is noisiest, so the same instant read 179 on one arm and 146 on the other. Under 2 cm of landmark noise the elbow config counted the clip's 3 reps correctly 25% of the time and over-counted to 4-7 the rest; this one counts 3 every time, and 92% of the time at 3 cm. The elbow-shoulder-hip angle lies in the frontal plane, which a front-framed camera sees square on, so depth barely enters it. TOP is racked at <=75, BOTTOM is locked out at >=145.

stage._note: Keypoints 13-11-23 / 14-12-24 (elbow-shoulder-hip), 3D world angle, better-seen side. Rest measured on the player 6 Sep 2026, off 2226 logged frames of a real set: they rack with the upper arms roughly level, and the bottom between reps read 51-91 depending on the rep. At rest<75, taken from the reference animation whose rack sits at 55, three of seven full lockouts were refused for never re-arming - every one of them peaked above 159, so they were good presses thrown away by a threshold measured on a drawing. At <95 all seven count, and replaying those frames with gaussian angle noise it still counts seven at every level up to 6 degrees. The reference clip counts three either way. Count at >135 sits 14.7 degrees under the weakest lockout and 30 above the lateral raise's 105 ceiling, so a raise on the same joint triple can never register as a press. The wrist-above-shoulder check separates a press overhead from an arm swung out behind. Ceiling 180: the arm does not go past straight in line with the torso. Rest is a band, not a half-line: <95 is how high the bottom may be before the counter will not re-arm, >70 is how low it may go before the arm has put the weight down instead of racking it. The player asked for the 70 knowing what it costs -- on the logged set they racked at a median of 48 and only 2 of 13 reps cleared it, so this is a rule about how the press should be done, not a description of how it was. The elbow floor (>70, shoulder-elbow-wrist) is the same rule read at the other joint; on the logged set it refused none.

tempo._note: measured window: topExit crossing -> bottomEnter crossing, not the full descent

cues.enter: Face the camera, hands at shoulder height, upper arms down by your sides.
cues.tooHigh: Press all the way up — arms overhead, in line with your torso.
cues.tooFast: Lower the hands back to the shoulders under control.
cues.gate: Rack at your shoulders — don't drop your arms past them, and press straight overhead.
cues.framing: I can't see your hands — step back.
